jules: Hey team — started getting a sudden spike of 429s from customers using rwd3-extended around 09:12 UTC. They call it out as 'rate_limited' in the response body even though overall account tpm looks fine. Context lengths around 96k tokens, fanout prefetch pattern, ~100 concurrent prefetch requests per user :confused:
ingrid_support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste a repro curl (sanitized) and one raw 429 response body? Also which model exact name + variant?
jules: Repro below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-extended-v2","input":"<~96k tokens payload truncated>","stream":false}'
```
One 429 body we captured: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"per_model_tpm_exceeded","retry_after":0.8,"limit":"model_tpm","request_id":"req_8f3a2c"}`
mike_sre: Thanks — two quick hypotheses: (1) this is hitting per-model TPM (not per-account) because rwd3-extended has much higher token cost and the fanout multiplies token submission; (2) the long context means each request consumes more token-units toward TPM, and bursts cause the model's short window quota to trip.
eva_eng: To add — we also saw fallback behavior where the request queueing at the model shard returns 429 when queue > 200ms. That shows up as `per_model_concurrency` in older logs. Can you grep for request_id req_8f3a2c in your logs? It should have a route header `x-rwd-model-shard` with the shard id.
jules: Found it: `x-rwd-model-shard: shard-b-7`, and full server trace with timings attached: `request_id=req_8f3a2c path=/v1/generate queued_ms=235 execute_ms=1200 token_cost=18400` — queued_ms spikes right before 429.
ryan-ml: That `token_cost=18400` number is the key. Our accounting counts tokens towards TPM at model-level. 18.4k token-cost per request * 100 concurrent = 1.84M token units over short window -> easily exceeds per-model short-window TPM cap.
ingrid_support: OK — customer says they need to prefetch replies for UX. Proposed mitigations: reduce simultaneous prefetch concurrency, enable prefix-KV caching (if applicable), or shard prefetches across model variants (rwd3-extended -> rwd3-extended-lite for prefetch). We can also temporarily bump their per-model tpm for a support-assisted window.
mike_sre: Practical quick steps to repro and validate: 1) Run curl loop at lower concurrency to see when 429s stop: use `seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P16 -I{} curl ...` 2) Observe `queued_ms` and `token_cost` in logs; 3) try switching to streaming mode to reduce peak token accounting per request.
jules: Tried xargs test — below shows 50 concurrent workers -> 30% 429s; with P=8 -> 2% 429s. Confirmed concurrency sensitivity.
ryan-ml: Long-term we recommend: (a) batching small prefetches into one request where possible; (b) use a lower-cost variant for prefetch; (c) implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect `retry_after` in body. Example retry header handling in JS snippet:```js
async function callWithBackoff(req){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if(res.status!==429) return res;
    const body = await res.json();
    const wait = (body.retry_after || (0.5 * Math.pow(2,i))) * 1000;
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait + Math.random()*200));
  }
  throw new Error('rate limited');
}
```
ingrid_support: Support action: I can open a temporary, scoped per-model tpm increase for the customer while they implement mitigations. Need: customer org id, expected sustained tpm during window, and an ETA for changes.
eva_eng: Also flagging an infra tweak: consider raising per-shard queue threshold alerts for shard-b-7 — it hit queue >200ms frequently. I'll add a short-run dashboard panel for shard-b-7 queued_ms percentiles.
jules: Customer org id: org_98765. They ask for a 24-48h increase to handle migration (target sustained ~300k token-units/min). ETA for code changes: ~36h.
mike_sre: Fine — Ingrid, please file the temporary quota change and include the shard traces and token_cost stats. I’ll follow up to confirm we didn’t miss a routing bug.
ryan-ml: One gotcha to call out — context-length throttles can also flip behavior if you include large system prompts in every prefetch. Consider keeping a small system prompt + cached KV to avoid re-sending static context.
ingrid_support: Filed escalation ticket #ES-2026 with engineering attached. Tentative plan: temp per-model tpm increase until 2026-03-19T22:00Z, customer to rollout prefetch sharding/retries in 36h, infra to monitor shard queue. :thumbsup:
mike_sre: Thanks everyone. If we see the 429 rate drop after the quota bump + backoff, we’ll close. If not, we’ll dig deeper into model-side qos. :eyes:
